An internal guard, as its message says ('Internal error'): each request position is looked up once, so the database returns at most one row for it unless the dialect's statement is wrong. The core keeps the same guard (sql.rs, request_order). It is reachable only by a sampler made to return a row twice, as `tests/determinism/test_determinism_batch.py::test_the_entity_rows_of_a_query`, `tests/determinism/test_determinism_batch.py::test_the_entity_rows_of_a_subgraph`, `tests/determinism/test_determinism_batch.py::test_the_rows_a_foreign_key_points_at` do.

Live backend only. A column with an expression, and so without a physical source column, reaches a SQL sampler from sdm_client in two ways. A Databricks metric view or a Snowflake semantic view keeps a view's column expression (sdm_client/materializers/sources.py:235-260 builds the graph with Graph.from_databricks_metric_view or from_snowflake_semantic_view, which keep it at rfm/graph.py:1275-1286 and 1625-1640); _view_expr_message (rfm/graph.py:177-207) keeps an expression without function calls even when trust_expressions is false. Those views are reached only through a live warehouse, and no recorded transcript asks of one (the brief allows no live access in this phase). The other way, a composite key's derived column named __kumo_key_... (base/composite_key.py:31), is refused with every column of the reserved __kumo_ prefix while the SQL sampler is made (base/sql_sampler.py:36-62), before this line; the driver fixture duckdb-a-pair-of-key-columns records that refusal, which is itself a Python bug: a composite key cannot be sampled on a SQL source. sdm_client makes no other column with an expression. So the core's port of these lines (SqlBackend::new, driver/sql.rs:138-174) is not compared with today's Python offline; a live run on a view compares it. Offline it is reachable only by skipping the reserved-prefix refusal, as `tests/rust_core/rfm/test_driver_fixtures.py::test_the_core_runs_what_the_engine_runs[duckdb-a-pair-of-key-columns]` does (test_driver_fixtures.py:278-284).
